title: Lakh-Thiahane au Poisson Sec
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik)
desc: A very thick savoury millet porridge: an onion browned with dried fish and tomato paste, pounded onions and chilli, then 3 litres of boiling water, ground raw peanuts for a quarter of an hour, and sankhal for another quarter of an hour.
longDesc: The savoury register of lakh, which the dessert-leaning sources miss. An onion is browned in peanut oil with the dried fish; tomato paste is dissolved in a little water; the two remaining onions are pounded with the chilli and added. Raw peanuts are pounded and sieved into flour. Three litres of boiling water are added, and as soon as it boils again the peanut flour goes in with stirring; cover and cook a quarter of an hour; add the sankhal (millet semolina) and cook another quarter of an hour. Serve lukewarm. It should be very thick, ‘like a sort of soup’ — as printed.
ingredients: 1 piece of dried fish — quantity not printed
steps: In a pot, brown one sliced onion in peanut oil with the dried fish. Add the tomato paste and dilute with a little water.
In a mortar, pound the other two onions with the chilli to form a paste and add it to the pot.
Pound the raw peanuts and sieve them to get a flour.
Pour 3 litres of boiling water into the pot and salt. As soon as it boils again, add the peanut flour, stirring. Cover and cook for a quarter of an hour.
Add the sankhal and continue cooking another quarter of an hour.
Serve lukewarm, peppered. It should be very thick, like a sort of soup.
chefTips: The printed cue is ‘dès qu’elle bout de nouveau’ — as soon as it boils again — before adding the peanut flour.
Stir continuously when the flour goes in to avoid lumps.
The page’s ‘Courir’ in the method is a near-certain misprint for ‘couvrir’ (cover); reported in the sources.
commonMistakes: Adding the flour to water that is not boiling.
Letting it set cold and thick before serving.
Skipping the pounding of the onions into a paste.
healthBenefits: Peanuts and millet provide protein and fibre.
culturalNote: Savoura’s page sits beside her dessert lakh and shows the dish in its savoury form — a thick peanut-millet meal built on dried fish, tomato and chilli.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Lakh-thiahane au poisson sec’. Byline: Amina Savoura. Publication: Afrik (afrik.com). Date: ‘Publié le 22 août 2012 à 10h23’, ‘mis à jour le 6 avril 2026 à 09h39’. Yield: none printed (8 used for scheduling). SINGLE-PASS.

MISPRINTS as printed, not corrected: ‘Courir et laisser cuire un quart d’heure’ (near-certainly ‘couvrir’); ‘eau bouillantes’; ‘elle boue’ for ‘elle bout’. Cues in fragments: ‘dès qu’elle boue de nouveau’; ‘Cela doit être très épais, comme une sorte de soupe’.
ABSENT, not estimated: the dried-fish quantity and the oil quantity. Prep and cook are the printed two quarter-hours plus scheduling estimates.
